title: Evaluation of 3D Markerless Motion Capture Accuracy Using OpenPose With Multiple Video Cameras
metricDefinition: OpenPose keypoints from multiple cameras are reconstructed in 3D and compared with marker-based joint positions; errors describe measurement accuracy.

extractionLocations.description: Camera, OpenPose keypoint, calibration, and reconstruction procedure.
Joint-position errors retained only as measurement limitations.

study.deviceAndEnvironment: Five synchronized cameras and laboratory reference motion capture

measurements.definition: Difference between OpenPose-based and marker-based joint positions over movement intervals.
measurements.calculationMethod: Mean absolute error across corresponding 3D joint-position time series.
notes: Accuracy results must not become posture behavior limits.

reportedFindings.summary: Tracking failures and joint-position errors vary by task and capture condition, supporting explicit quality gating.

faceFitMappings.reason: The study supports measuring pose reliability but does not define Face-Fit available-frame ratio.

thresholdAssessment.reason: Joint-position errors are algorithm validity results, not acceptable interview posture.

limitations: Multi-camera 3D sports tasks do not match a seated single-webcam interview.
Quality availability may gate measurement only and must not penalize behavior.
